Measure m125 at 1/1, 100 uL sample and 300 uL DCM; predicted V1/V2 is 10.80/28.99 mL. The 300-uL protocol measured 9.25/18.35 at 50 uL in 00043aebb2540e369a7b and 7.30/20.23 at 150 uL in 03744855d469f4cca7e6. This midpoint, paired with the selected 500-uL protocol, tests whether the large completion difference persists between the measured amount endpoints.

Measure the matched m125 1/1, 100-uL sample experiment in 500 uL DCM; predicted 10.64/29.10 mL, almost identical to the selected 300-uL prediction. Yet f4fb5c03b8e8996e75f6 and 9bd998a328b109ef639e finish at 36.14 and 39.38 mL at 50 and 150 uL. The pair can teach an association that remains poorly represented without attributing it causally to loading volume alone.

Measure m177 at 5/1 and 150 uL; predicted 4.97/17.34 mL. The new 10/1 high-amount result aef5cafc63ca445e92fa finishes at 46.72 mL, versus 20.70 for 100 uL in ce14dd2481560a984aea. At 5/1, the measured 50- and 100-uL completions are 14.51 and 19.18 in 27bac953781c17a3a74b and 08812206a257481691c4. This locates the stronger-solvent boundary of prolonged high-amount completion.

Measure m92 at 20/1, 100 uL sample and 200 uL EA; predicted 9.31/26.64 mL. At this ratio, 66da447ca0fe7160cc1c measured 13.96/34.55 at 50 uL, whereas e9dc948c0e68a88eb621 measured 5.42/21.38 at 150 uL. The midpoint distinguishes a gradual amount response from a sharper transition or record-specific variation and constrains both endpoints within this dicarbonyl environment.

Acquire another m92 1/1, 50-uL sample record with 200 uL EA loading solvent; predicted 6.11/16.08 mL. The same recorded EA tuple in 00a89de0e6cc7377a84b measured 5.18/12.01, while the PE-loading counterpart e626b5b8083ea1fd02f2 measured 8.02/20.57. An additional catalog record tests whether the EA result recurs before generalizing a solvent effect. It is not presumed to be a controlled technical replicate.

Measure m45 at 20/1 and 100 uL; predicted 38.91/67.78 mL. The 50/1, 100-uL record 129036e0bccc4ff7e848 has near-zero, reversed measured endpoints and cannot establish a physically valid early-elution interval. The adjacent 20/1 low-amount record b24f66ff77974f8ba6e1 measured 39.58/65.65. This checks whether ordinary weak-solvent retention persists at the same sample amount as the anomalous record; it cannot directly verify that 50/1 record.

Measure phosphorus-containing m202 at 1/1 and 100 uL. Its current predicted endpoints are reversed, 4.65/4.46 mL. Recent reversed ester predictions in 1ac98da1ee548520f15b and 2631e65cfde93b7bbd64 produced ordered measured intervals, while cb446680f62351d087a9 exposed substantial overprediction for m202 at 10/1. This tests strong-solvent endpoint transfer beyond the ester family and supplies a label in a concrete consistency-failure region.

Measure m73 in neat EA at 100 uL; predicted 5.16/8.97 mL. Its approximately matched 1/1 record 2cf789c87f7c6325c020 measured 18.60/18.96, whereas 2/1 and 5/1 records 49932dbd3d16bb64f71a and c9a9fab963b85f141aa6 measured 5.26/11.60 and 5.63/13.55. This tests the predicted return to early elution and bounds the unusual 1/1 pattern without imposing a universal monotone solvent curve.

Measure ether-containing acrylate m21 at 1/1 and 50 uL; predicted 7.94/9.00 mL. The recent matched-amount 10/1 record 487606cee9b08ded91f3 measured 7.17/11.35, weakening the earlier predicted onset increase at that ratio. This stronger-solvent point tests the currently predicted narrow interval and different responses of onset and completion. It complements the m73 experiment with a distinct ester environment.

Measure meta-methylacetophenone m41 at 50/1 and 100 uL; predicted 16.61/33.32 mL. At 100 uL and DCM loading, ortho-methyl m44 in 4dc668dc01885a313d70 measured 19.44/26.13, while dimethyl m33 in d2c44b46eb306c56f241 measured 8.49/38.59. Densities differ slightly. This comparison tests how aromatic substitution changes onset and completion separately in a well-populated ketone family.

Measure tertiary alcohol m51 at 5/1 and 50 uL; predicted 16.74/30.26 mL. Existing m51 observations at 2/1 and 10/1, a95a211366968c4cd1f0f and 19229d505f75d05a0bcb, leave this intermediate ratio uncovered. Together with the selected 150-uL experiment, this tests the predicted small amount response in a sterically crowded alcohol rather than transferring loading behavior directly from less hindered alcohols.

Measure the matched m51 5/1 experiment at 150 uL; predicted 16.07/30.84 mL. The selected pair predicts only about 0.67 mL earlier onset and 0.58 mL later completion at higher amount. By comparison, primary alcohol m204 at 5/1 showed a much larger onset decrease with nearly unchanged completion in 45a1b11ae63f2dab2e48 and 1211905ebc8972913270. The pair tests whether structural environment attenuates that response.

Measure para-aminoacetophenone m36 at 1/1 and 50 uL; predicted 11.47/23.20 mL. Its 2/1, 100-uL observation 6b7209c2e8154837a8c7 measured 22.32/39.86. This adds a stronger-solvent anchor for an amino-carbonyl environment, complementing pending quinoline coverage and abundant neutral ketones. Amine-silica interactions are a chemical prior; the ratio and amount both differ from the reference, so this is a transfer test rather than an isolated solvent contrast.

Measure dibenzylamine m212 in neat EA at 100 uL; predicted 8.06/17.01 mL. Paired with the selected 1/1 experiment, it tests the predicted increase in completion under the stronger mobile phase while holding recorded loading conditions fixed. The 2/1 reference 6defbf00ecb558b77d50 measured 8.75/16.75. Its crossed V2 quantiles make the nominal quantile span unsuitable as a confidence signal; the acquisition is motivated by the response shape.

Measure m212 at 1/1 and 100 uL; predicted 8.89/13.67 mL. Together with the selected neat-EA point and measured 2/1 reference 6defbf00ecb558b77d50, this tests a predicted completion minimum at 1/1. The much different 5/1 low- and middle-amount records d5234e966aa231be05e5 and 252c027cf5a42b92c953 make amount matching consequential. The pair can distinguish a shared basic-compound solvent trend from a local condition pattern.

Measure isobutyl benzoate m56 at 50/1 and 150 uL; predicted 7.39/20.66 mL. The recent same-amount 100/1 observation e7c4d856d4d9a8d5ddbf measured 6.80/25.46 and had an acquisition-time V2 underestimate of 9.19 mL. This intermediate weak-solvent point tests how completion extends while onset remains early, complementing the pending 20/1 low-amount experiment without assuming its outcome.

hypotheses.content: Amount responses depend on molecule, mobile-phase strength and endpoint. The positive response of m211 at 50/1 does not transfer to 10/1, and m199 shows decreases at both neat EA and 2/1. Large responses in some families therefore do not justify a universal loading slope.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched contrasts can teach when a small amount response is appropriate and when onset, completion or both require substantial corrections. Intermediate amounts can reveal curvature that endpoint pairs cannot establish.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m51 5/1 pair support its predicted small amount response, and does the m92 20/1 midpoint interpolate smoothly between its measured amount endpoints?

hypotheses.content: m125 has protocol-associated completion differences at 2/1, 1/1 and neat EA. The proposed convergence in neat EA is contradicted by the latest matched-amount comparison. Onset differences vary with conditions, so a constant offset for both endpoints is inadequate. Loading volume alone is not established as the cause.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Current matched predictions still differ negligibly despite multiple measured completion differences. Midpoint labels can constrain each protocol's amount response and reduce averaging across distinct recorded-condition associations.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 1/1 and 100 uL sample, do the two protocols retain the completion difference seen at both 50 and 150 uL?

hypotheses.content: Catalog records sharing all recorded conditions can have substantially different outcomes. The short m84 40/1, 100-uL interval did not recur, so it does not establish a reproducible high-amount contraction. m92's single EA-versus-PE contrast may likewise combine protocol dependence with between-record variability.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Additional same-tuple catalog labels can prevent isolated outcomes from being interpreted as deterministic loading or solvent effects. They also characterize predictive limits imposed by information absent from the catalog.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does another m92 1/1 EA-loading record reproduce the original 12.01-mL completion or move toward the 20.57-mL PE-loading observation?

hypotheses.content: m73's 1/1 records at both 50 and 100 uL show later onset and completion than its measured 2/1 and 5/1 series. Whether this pattern is localized to 1/1, followed by the predicted return to early elution in neat EA, remains unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: This is a measured exception to a simple monotone solvent-strength prior. A boundary label can constrain how narrowly the model should represent that exception instead of extending it across stronger-solvent ester rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 100 uL in neat EA, does m73 return near the predicted 5.16/8.97 mL or retain substantially later elution?

hypotheses.content: m177 has high-amount completion differences at 10/1, 20/1 and 50/1, with onset much less affected at 10/1. The latest 150-uL 10/1 result supports extension of prolonged completion beyond 20/1. Its stronger-solvent boundary and reproducibility remain unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The 10/1 acquisition predicted onset accurately but underestimated completion by 24.86 mL. A same-amount solvent bridge can teach endpoint-specific condition dependence without propagating the exceptional low-amount 20/1 interval across the family.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does 150 uL at 5/1 finish near the measured lower-amount 14.51-19.18 mL range or retain substantially prolonged completion?

hypotheses.content: The near-zero, reversed m45 50/1 endpoints may be a localized record pattern rather than evidence of a broad collapse of weak-solvent acid retention. Reporting differences or unrecorded experimental circumstances are possible explanations, but none is established.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest record generated a very large acquisition error but violates the stated endpoint interpretation. A neighboring label can constrain its influence on the acid response curve, while the catalog alone cannot diagnose the record's origin.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m45 at 20/1 and the same 100-uL sample amount retain the long interval suggested by the measured 50-uL 20/1 result?

feedback_interpretation: The latest m125 results strengthen the protocol association and reject the proposed neat-EA convergence: at 1/1 and 150 uL, completion was 20.23 versus 39.38 mL for 300 versus 500 uL DCM, and at neat EA and 100 uL it was 11.22 versus 22.11. The current predictor still nearly equates the protocols, motivating a matched midpoint pair. For m84, the second 40/1, 100-uL record finished at 24.10 rather than 4.45 mL; the additional 50-uL record finished at 19.20. This rejects using the original short record as evidence of a reproducible negative loading effect, and I pause m84 acquisitions. It also makes reproducibility a necessary question for the new m92 loading-solvent contrast. m211 at 10/1 shows only a modest onset decrease and little completion change with amount, unlike its positive response at 50/1. m199's endpoint decreases recur at 2/1. These support conditional loading responses. m92 at 20/1 shows substantial differences between 50 and 150 uL, motivating a midpoint rather than a shared solvent-curve correction. m177 at 10/1 and 150 uL finished at 46.72 mL despite accurately predicted onset, supporting an endpoint-specific completion problem and motivating the 5/1 boundary measurement. The m181 20/1 high-amount bridge has similar completion to its 100-uL observation, so it does not explain away its weak-solvent extension as an amount effect. m104's 10/1 bridge lies near its measured 20/1 endpoints; I do not extend its short 50/1 observation into a general correction. m21's 10/1 label weakens the predicted onset rise there. Both ester endpoint-order checks measured ordinary ordered intervals; a remaining m202 reversal is therefore a useful functional-group extension. Finally, m45's negative completion is an observed label inconsistency, not a finding of valid near-zero retention. All stated prediction errors are acquisition-time errors.
batch_rationale: The pending batch already covers several neutral aromatic and carbonyl conditions, strong-solvent quinoline and fluoroaldehyde points, and a benzoate solvent extension. These supplements answer additional questions that those labels cannot resolve. The m125 pair addresses a persistent representation failure; the m177 experiment locates the boundary of a large completion-specific discrepancy. The m92 midpoint and matched m51 pair test conditional loading relationships, while the extra m92 catalog record guards against mistaking variability for a transferable protocol effect. The m73, m21 and m212 experiments test distinct strong-solvent response shapes, including measured and predicted nonmonotonic patterns. m36 adds an amino-carbonyl anchor, m41 supports a close aryl-ketone structural comparison, and m56 constrains weak-solvent completion after recent feedback. One m202 experiment targets reversed predicted endpoints, and one neighboring m45 experiment investigates the scope of an inconsistent measured record. Repeated molecules serve explicit comparisons; no selected row is treated as having a known error before measurement. The expected benefit is better learning of endpoint-specific structure-condition relationships across the Row-distribution. Quantile spans are single-predictor diagnostics, sometimes crossed, and are not treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty. Elution interval width remains a measured outcome.
